decision.title: How far should Aperture House rebuild marketing around AI?

sources.claim: The plan changes the marketing operating model across eight roles and a synthetic £1.2m annual budget.
The current scorecard rewards output volume, cadence and deadlines. It does not measure customer usefulness or independent quality judgement.
Seven of ten synthetic customers remembered the clear category point of view. Two remembered the recent campaign theme.
Make quality clear without killing surprise.
Maya makes her sharpest judgements by comparing real alternatives, not by grading one abstract proposal.
Maya is willing to delegate generation. The unresolved issue is whether another person can notice and preserve the quality signals she sees.
Changing role names without changing decision rights can preserve the old approval bottleneck. This synthetic fixture does not claim a causal rate.
The later launch preparation initially assigns final approval to the marketing lead and treats weekly and launch work alike.

question.prompt: If the pilot ships more work but Maya still has to redo the final version, has it worked?

options.label: No
options.effect: The first gate becomes independent launch quality, not output volume.

options.label: Only if the rewrites fall quickly
options.effect: The first gate tracks how much final rescue falls across three live launches.

options.label: Yes, if customers prefer the work
options.effect: The first gate becomes blinded customer preference, with Maya's rewrite load kept as a risk signal.

routes.label: Rebuild now
routes.summary: Replace the current production model with a small AI-native team this quarter.
routes.strength: Exposes the real work and decision rights quickly.
routes.risk: May scale output before Maya's standard can be applied without her.

routes.label: Prove the system first
routes.summary: Run one important campaign through a separate AI-native route before redesigning roles.
routes.strength: Tests the operating model and Maya's quality standard together.
routes.risk: Becomes theatre if it keeps the old scorecard or has no authority to work differently.

routes.label: Add tools gradually
routes.summary: Keep the current team and add AI inside each existing role.
routes.risk: May preserve the work, measures and approval bottleneck that need to change.

ownedCall.decision: Prove the new system on one important campaign before rebuilding the whole function.
ownedCall.firstGate: A non-founder lead ships launch work Maya would approve without rewriting, while blinded customer preference holds or improves.
ownedCall.killCondition: Stop if the pilot only increases output, still needs Maya's final rescue, or cannot show fresh customer evidence.

proposal.text: Maya keeps the final review for all marketing work.

corrected.text: Maya keeps the final call on launch work. Weekly work can use the agreed quality check.

rejected.text: Maya keeps the final review for all marketing work.

laterPreparation.before: Final approval: Marketing lead. Weekly work and launch work use the same quality check.
laterPreparation.after: Final approval for launch work: Maya. Weekly work uses the agreed quality check without Maya's final review.
